Focus on TTFT (time-to-first-token) differences with streaming vs non-streaming, sequence length tradeoffs, and kernel choices/quantization. SE presented recent benchmarks showing TTFT improvements with streaming and lighter kernels; customer had questions around memory/kv cache behavior and worst-case p95 latency. transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-10-06 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Rohit (Redwood SRE Consultant), Jordan (Novapay Eng Mgr), Priya (Novapay SRE), Samir (Novapay ML Eng), Lena (Novapay PM)

Summary: quick sync on latency tuning; run benchmarks; agree owner for enabling prefix caching; share kernel mapping

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick roll call — we got jordan, priya, samir, lena from novapay?
[00:06] Jordan: yeah, hey alex, hey maya, hi rohit. all here.
[00:09] Maya: hey folks. we'll keep this focused on the TTFT and streaming numbers we ran this week.
[00:15] Priya: yay, excited. last week we saw spikes at p95 when seq > 256 so curious what you found.
[00:21] Maya: right, ok so i'll share my screen — i put together a small table — but high level: enabling streaming dropped TTFT by ~40-55% on our 1xA100 baseline for seq 128 and 256. for seq 512 the improvement was smaller, about 25%. p95 improvements were more modest, and we still see tail events tied to kernel fallback.
[00:40] Samir: when you say streaming did the tokens arrive chunked? like were you using a 1-token early flush or 8-token windows?
[00:47] Maya: good q. we used a 4-token chunk size in the test. that gives best balance between network overhead and early tokenization. also used continuous kv cache so subsequent chunks didn't re-embed prefixes.
[00:58] Jordan: ok, that matches what we've tried. one thing — our app needs first token under 220ms 95% of the time for live assist; last week we were hitting 320ms at p95 on 256.
[01:08] Alex: understood — goal is clear. two notes: 1) streaming mainly helps TTFT because you can pipeline token generation and network send, 2) kernel choices and quantization affect both TTFT and p95.
[01:20] Rohit: quick practical: for kernel fallback we saw some NVidia triton-ish fallbacks when certain attention kernels hit memory pressure; that creates spikes. maya, did you see kernel reassignments?
[01:30] Maya: yes, on seq512 we observed fallback to a slower attention kernel about 8% of the time in our runs — that correlated with p99 spikes. i noted those in the spreadsheet i uploaded (link in chat). there's also a mis-transcribed line in that doc where it says "KV cash" instead of cache, haha.
[01:45] Priya: ha, typos everywhere. can you summarize what triggers the fallback? memory, batch size, or prompt length?
[01:52] Maya: it's mainly peak memory + certain model operators that don't have fused kernels for long sequences. so when effective batch*seq crosses a threshold the runtime picks a compatibility kernel. lowering batch or enabling quantization/trimmed kernels helps.
[02:06] Samir: what about quantization? we tried int8 last month but saw a quality drop on some finance prompts. is there a middle ground?
[02:13] Maya: yeah we recommend mixed int8/FP16 profiles; for QAT-sensitive prompts you can pick a hybrid where attention stays FP16 and linear layers int8. we've added recommended profiles in the kernel mapping sheet.
[02:24] Jordan: any idea on the impact on TTFT specifically for those hybrid profiles?
[02:28] Maya: smaller than full int8 but still a 10-15% win vs full FP16 for token generation compute. TTFT gains are mostly compute-bound — so lighter kernels help.
[02:40] Lena: i'd like to understand prefix caching — we heard enabling it can reduce cost a lot, but does it affect TTFT?
[02:47] Rohit: prefix caching helps subsequent requests — if the prompt prefix is stable it caches KV and avoids re-encoding. TTFT for first cold request doesn't change, but for warmed flows you can see huge reductions in both TTFT and p95.
[02:58] Priya: our traffic pattern has many repetitive templates, so this could help quickly. how hard is it to enable in staging?
[03:03] Maya: should be straightforward — toggle in the request options and set cache key strategy; i'll send a snippet. there are some gotchas around memory retention and eviction so set a TTL and size cap.
[03:16] Jordan: ok please share the snippet.
[03:18] Alex: we'll add that to action items. next i want to go through a specific run — maya, can you call out the numbers for seq128, 256, 512 streaming vs non-streaming?
[03:27] Maya: sure. seq128 non-streaming TTFT median ~85ms, p95 ~210ms. seq128 streaming TTFT median ~45ms, p95 ~150ms. seq256 non-streaming median ~120ms p95 ~320ms; seq256 streaming median ~70ms p95 ~240ms. seq512 non-streaming median ~200ms p95 ~480ms; seq512 streaming median ~150ms p95 ~360ms. again p95 is still influenced by kernel fallback.
[03:56] Samir: those are helpful. so streaming gives solid TTFT wins but doesn't fully fix p95. do you have per-request traces where fallback lines up?
[04:06] Maya: yes uploaded. in trace we saw a batch that triggered a fallback due to a 3x spike in intermediate memory (we think due to a long prompt plus batch coalescing). we can reproduce if we artificially increase concurrency in staging.
[04:20] Priya: concurrency — we plan to run 100 rps in staging to mimic peak. do you recommend lowering batch window to avoid coalescing?
[04:28] Maya: you can reduce max batch size and enable early flush thresholds; that reduces probability of hitting the kernel threshold but increases per-token overhead. it's a tradeoff. for Novapay's latency SLO i'd suggest smaller batch windows with streaming enabled and prefix caching where possible.
[04:41] Jordan: does dedicated reduce these fallbacks?
[04:44] Rohit: dedicated predictable memory helps — less noisy neighbors so kernel planners can pick the fastest kernels more reliably. also with dedicated you can pick a hardware SKU tuned for long sequences.
[04:55] Alex: and Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and routing policies; if latency SLO is critical we can scope a dedicated footprint in the next call.
[05:03] Lena: cost question — how much more for dedicated?
[05:06] Alex: i'll send pricing bands in the follow-up; depends on commit. action item for me.
[05:11] Priya: security side — anything streaming changes for data residency or logs?
[05:15] Maya: streaming doesn't change retention or residency — payloads and logs are controlled by the same retention/KMS policies. we log request/response frames if enabled, but obviously can opt out.
[05:26] Samir: quick note — in some of your slides i saw mention of kernel selection heuristics, can you explain how runtime chooses kernels?
[05:33] Maya: sure — runtime profiles model ops and sequence distribution, then picks kernels based on latency-cost models; it may choose a fused attention kernel for seq<=256, otherwise use a fallback that uses less memory but higher compute. there's also an option to pin kernel choices per deployment if you want deterministic behavior.
[05:51] Jordan: pinning sounds appealing since we want stable p95. is that a config change?
[05:55] Maya: yes, we can set kernel_policy: pinned in the deployment config; downside is you might lose some automatic improvements but you gain predictability.
[06:04] Priya: can pinning force the fast kernel even if memory is high and cause OOM?
[06:08] Rohit: pinning will error if the kernel can't be scheduled; runtime will surface that as an allocation failure, it's safer than silently falling back.
[06:18] Alex: ok, quick checkpoint — agreed actions: maya runs streaming benchmarks at 128/256/512, priya enables prefix caching in staging, alex sends pricing and next meeting. any other blockers?
[06:29] Jordan: curious about eval quality impact from quantization — we need to run our finance prompts through hybrid profiles. samir will own that.
[06:35] Samir: yep i'll run the evals and compare rouge/accuracy on the paired prompts; will share by friday.
[06:41] Maya: also note we observed about 12% CPU bump on the host when streaming is enabled due to increased RPCs; fine for most skus but call it out.
[06:52] Priya: thanks — we'll check host metrics.
[06:55] Alex: anything on routing/policy? we mentioned fallback routing to a smaller model if latency spikes — should we consider that?
[07:03] Jordan: possible but prefer keep same model unless we must degrade. would rather tune infra first.
[07:09] Maya: we can demo an A/B route fallback but it requires careful evaluation on regression.
[07:14] Lena: timeline question — we want pilot decision by end of month. is that realistic?
[07:18] Alex: yes if benchmarks and prefix caching show p95 < 220ms for 256 we can propose next steps for Dedicated by mid-Oct and final decision end of month.
[07:27] Priya: ok good.
[07:29] Alex: any more questions?
[07:31] Jordan: one small nit — in the spreadsheet some kernel names were munged, eg "fused-attn-v2" became "fuse-attn-vtwo" in transcription. not a big deal but please clean.
[07:40] Maya: will clean and re-upload.
[07:42] Samir: can you also include the exact test harness commands? we want deterministic runs.
[07:46] Maya: yes i'll include the harness commands and a docker image sha.
[07:50] Alex: great. let's recap next steps then close.
